question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in outbound recipient allowlist for Slack DMs, and should that policy be Slack-specific or a shared channel/plugin contract?
rationale: This changes a recipient authorization boundary and adds public config surface, so automation should not pick defaults, owner boundary, or fail-open/fail-closed behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve opt-in Slack outbound policy
options.body: Add a Slack-owned outbound recipient allowlist with current behavior preserved unless explicitly configured, plus docs, diagnostics, logging, and send-path tests.

options.title: Design shared channel policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a generic outbound recipient-policy contract for multiple DM-capable channels and plugin SDK behavior.

options.title: Keep policy in agent instructions
options.body: Decline a technical allowlist for now and document that outbound DMs remain governed by operator prompts, permissions, and Slack workspace controls.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in Slack outbound policy
recommendation.body: Add a Slack-owned outbound recipient allowlist with current behavior preserved unless explicitly configured, plus docs, diagnostics, logging, and send-path tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and shared outbound ownership, and steipete has the strongest sampled history across those surfaces.
